name: urdulens
description: Open, reproducible benchmark that compares OCR engines on Urdu text lines, with a weekly automated leaderboard, a synthetic data generator, a trainable model and a photo reader app.

paragraphs: An open, reproducible benchmark for Urdu OCR: compare engines on the same lines, see where each one fails, and read Urdu from your own photos.

Urdu is written in cursive Nastaliq, and reading it from an image is still hard. Public Urdu OCR projects report very different error rates, each on its own data, so nobody can tell which approach is actually better:

Those numbers are self-reported on different, mostly undisclosed test sets, so they cannot be compared (checked September 2026; I could not find an open head-to-head benchmark, though my search was not exhaustive). UrduLens is a small, transparent attempt at a common yardstick: a frozen test set, a documented scoring method, engines behind one interface, a weekly automated run, and a public dashboard.
features: one fine-tuned TrOCR model reports a Tesseract word-recovery rate of 2.1% on its own data,
another TrOCR model reports a CER of about 25% on its validation set,
a vision-language model reports a CER of about 3% on its evaluation set.
